Typeset Figure Text

Source: R/figure-style.R
TypesetLabel.Rd

Applies manuscript typesetting to plain labels and returns rich text for 'gridtext'/'ggtext': italic P, q and n before = or <; powers of ten for 4.9e-04; superscript plus signs on markers (CD8+, FOXP3+, CD4 T, CD8 T); Treg/Tregs with subscript reg; log2; mm2; micrometres; italic gene symbols; and line breaks. Straight quotes stay straight (no typographic apostrophes).

Usage

TypesetLabel(
  x,
  genes = c("TP53", "RB1"),
  markers = c("CD\\d+[a-z]?", "FOXP3", "PD-L1", "PD-1", "Ki67", "MPO"),
  rich = .fig_has_rich_text()
)

Arguments

x

Character vector of labels.

genes

Gene symbols to set in italics.

markers

Marker names that take a superscript + when followed by +.

rich

If FALSE, return plain text with Unicode substitutes (superscript plus, subscript two, minus sign) instead of markup. The default uses markup when 'gridtext' and 'ggtext' are installed.

Value

Character vector of the same length.

Details

Typesetting can be switched off with options(phenoscapR.typeset = FALSE); labels are then only escaped for rich text. Single rules are switched off by naming them instead, for example options(phenoscapR.typeset = "treg"): "exponent", "p", "q", "n", "markers", "treg", "log2", "mm2", "um" and "genes". Figure specifications do this per figure, panel, text or legend ("typeset", see RenderFigure()).

Examples

TypesetLabel(c("p = 4.9e-04", "Tregs near CD8+ cells", "log2 ratio (mm2)"),
             rich = FALSE)
#> [1] "P = 4.9 × 10⁻⁴"             "Treg cells near CD8⁺ cells"
#> [3] "log₂ ratio (mm²)"
